stories.h: Russell Brand jailed for 10 and a half years for rape and sexual assaults
stories.p: British comedian Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison after a jury found him guilty of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others. He had denied the charges.
body: British comedian and actor Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison.
## The sentence

Brand, 51, was sentenced on Monday, 9 November 2026, after a jury of eight men and four women found him guilty of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others, in offences dating back to 2004. He was cleared of two counts of rape and one count of attempted indecent assault. Brand had maintained his innocence, saying all his encounters were consensual.
## The judge's remarks

Judge Joel Bennathan said Brand had shown a casual and arrogant disregard for women's right to say no, and placed the crimes in the context of his rise to fame about 20 years ago, when he was widely seen as clever, funny and charismatic.
## Background

Brand became famous in the 2000s as a stand-up comedian, television and radio presenter and Hollywood actor, and was known for his outrageous on-air behaviour and his public battles with drug and alcohol addiction. The allegations against him first emerged in a joint media investigation in 2023, after which he was charged by British police. In recent years he had reinvented himself as an online commentator with a large following.

stories.h: Odumodublvck says he refused to settle with man suing him over alleged assault
stories.p: Rapper Odumodublvck says a man who repeatedly filmed him without permission has taken him to court, accusing him of assault, and that he rejected his lawyers' advice to settle out of court.
body: Rapper Odumodublvck has spoken about a court case brought against him by a man he says repeatedly filmed him without permission.
## His account

According to reports on Monday, 9 November 2026, the rapper said the man gained access to his home through a mutual friend and began filming him without his consent, continuing even after warnings from him and his bouncer. He said the disagreement continued at a party when the man brought out his camera again, and that he confronted him on stage, but that they later settled their differences, with the man even dancing with him while still filming. Odumodublvck said he was surprised when the man later took him to court, accusing him of assault.
## Refusing to settle
The rapper said his lawyers advised him to settle the matter out of court, but he refused. The man's side of the story has not been reported, and the allegations have not been tested in court.
## Background
Odumodublvck, is an Abuja-based rapper known for hits such as 'Declan Rice'. He went viral last week after a brief encounter with Peter Obi at Abuja airport.

stories.h: Obi says NFF officials stopped him from greeting world champion Flamingos
stories.p: NDC candidate Peter Obi says Nigeria Football Federation officials refused to let him congratulate the Flamingos when he saw them at Abuja airport on their return with the U-17 World Cup trophy. The NFF had not responded.
body: Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), has accused officials of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) of stopping him from congratulating the Flamingos after their World Cup triumph.
## What Obi said

Obi said he was at the airport in Abuja at about 7am on Monday, 9 November 2026, to catch a flight to Enugu, when he saw the Flamingos, who had just arrived with the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup trophy. He said he asked his protocol officer to find out if he could go over and welcome the players, but was told that NFF officials had refused, reportedly warning that anyone who allowed him near the team would lose their job.
## 'Not the first time'

Obi said this was not the first time he had been prevented from supporting a national team. He recalled travelling to Uyo in March 2025 to watch a World Cup qualifier against Zimbabwe, and said that although he was warmly received before the match, he was not allowed the same access afterwards.
## Background

The Flamingos beat Japan 2-1 in the final in Rabat on Saturday to become the first African team to win the tournament, and were welcomed back to Nigeria on Monday. President Bola Tinubu and the First Lady have both congratulated the team.
## Presidency responds

The Presidency accused Obi of trying to politicise national sports teams. In a post on X on Monday, the President's special assistant on social media, Dada Olusegun, said the national teams, including the Under-17 girls, represent the whole country and not any party or individual's ambitions, and that protocol rules around national teams are designed to protect young athletes from political exploitation, commercial distractions and media pressure. The NFF itself had not publicly commented.
more: Obi says he saw the Flamingos at Abuja airport.

stories.h: Gospel singer Toluwanisings buried in Ibadan after family dispute
stories.p: Gospel singer Olayemi Bolaji, known as Toluwanisings, is being buried in Ibadan on Monday, almost four weeks after his death, following a dispute between his widow and his family that police helped resolve.
body: Gospel singer Olayemi Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, is being laid to rest in Ibadan, Oyo State, on Monday, 9 November 2026.
## The arrangements

According to funeral details shared on the singer's official Instagram page, the lying-in-state was scheduled for 9am to 10am, followed by a burial service from 10am to 11am at an event centre on Hope Road, Alakia, Ibadan. The announcement did not say where he would be interred.
## The dispute

Toluwanisings died in the early hours of 14 October 2026. His burial was delayed by weeks of disagreement between his widow and his family over the arrangements, reportedly including where he should be buried. The Oyo State Police Command stepped in after learning of the dispute on 28 October, with Commissioner of Police Olugbenga Abimbola helping the two sides reach an agreement.
## The burial

Videos from Monday's ceremony showed pallbearers in black suits carrying the singer's white casket, led by trumpeters, before he was taken to his home, where a private burial was held. Some fans remarked on the absence of fellow gospel artistes at the ceremony.
## Background
Toluwanisings was a Nigerian gospel singer. The public dispute over his burial attracted wide attention.

stories.h: Nigeria seeks $500m World Bank loan for infrastructure financing platform
stories.p: The federal government has approached the World Bank for a $500 million loan to set up a platform to attract private investment into infrastructure, part of a wider $3.85 billion programme called INFRAGROW.
body: The federal government has asked the World Bank for a $500 million loan to set up a platform to attract private investment into Nigerian infrastructure.
## The loan

According to a World Bank project document updated on 4 November 2026 and reported on Monday, 9 November, the facility is part of a broader $3.85 billion programme called the Nigeria Infrastructure Financing and De-Risking Platform for Growth and Jobs, or INFRAGROW. The Federal Ministry of Finance is listed as the borrower and the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority (NSIA) as the implementing agency. The aim is to reduce the risks that discourage private investors from funding infrastructure projects.
## Why the bank says it is needed

The World Bank estimates that Nigeria has an infrastructure financing gap of about $100 billion a year, which holds back growth, competitiveness and job creation. It says the problem is not only a lack of money but also weak project preparation and difficulty turning proposals into commercially viable investments.
## Atiku objects

ADC candidate Atiku Abubakar said on Tuesday, 10 November, that the government had no business taking on new debt on its way out. In a statement by his campaign spokesman, he said the World Bank was due to consider the loan on 25 May 2027, four days before the next presidential inauguration, and urged the bank not to approve it on that timetable and to publish its full terms, risks and repayment conditions first. The government has said the platform is needed to attract private investment into infrastructure.
## Background

The request comes as President Bola Tinubu also seeks Senate approval for about $7.7 billion in new external borrowing, and as government borrowing becomes a major campaign issue. NDC candidate Peter Obi has challenged the President to account for loans, while the Presidency says claims that it has borrowed ₦120 trillion are distorted. The World Bank reported last week that Nigeria's total external debt rose to about $145 billion in 2025.
more: The $500m loan is part of a $3.85bn programme.

stories.h: Hamzat vows to enforce one-year rent limit as Lagos governorship candidates debate
stories.p: Lagos APC governorship candidate Obafemi Hamzat says the state will enforce the legal limit on advance rent to one year, warning landlords against demanding two or three years upfront. He spoke at a televised governorship debate.
body: Lagos State Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat, the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for governor, says the state government will enforce the legal limit on advance rent payments.
## What he said

Speaking at a governorship debate organised by a coalition of media organisations on Sunday, 8 November 2026, Hamzat said the one-year cap on advance rent is already contained in the Lagos State Real Estate Registration Agency law passed in 2025, and that the focus now is making sure it is followed. He warned landlords against demanding two or three years' rent upfront, and said estate agents are required to register with the state and appear on an official database, urging residents to check it before dealing with agents.
## The law

The Lagos State Tenancy Law of 2011 already makes it unlawful for landlords or their agents to demand more than one year's rent in advance from a new tenant, and limits advance payments from sitting tenants. Despite this, demands for two or more years' rent have remained a widespread concern.
## Rhodes-Vivour's pitch

At the same debate, Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, the governorship candidate of the opposition ADC, said APC governments in Lagos had focused on policies that favoured the elite for more than 20 years, while residents of poorer and rural communities did not feel the benefit of the state's high revenue. He promised more than 100,000 housing units, a safer and cleaner state, and technology-driven measures to end flooding.
## Background

Hamzat is seeking to succeed Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu in the 2027 governorship election. Former governor Akinwunmi Ambode recently pledged to mobilise support for him. Housing costs are one of the biggest concerns for Lagos residents.
more: Hamzat says the one-year rent cap will be enforced.

He spoke at a televised governorship debate.

stories.h: CBN sets ₦15bn capital rule for dollar-backed stablecoins in new crypto rules
stories.p: The Central Bank of Nigeria has set minimum capital of ₦10 billion for naira-backed stablecoin issuers and ₦15 billion for those offering dollar or other foreign-currency tokens, under new rules for crypto operators. Other crypto service providers will need ₦1 billion.
body: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has introduced tougher rules for cryptocurrency and stablecoin businesses, including minimum capital requirements of up to ₦15 billion.
## The new requirements

Under the regulations, reported on Sunday, 8 November 2026, issuers of naira-backed stablecoins must have at least ₦10 billion in paid-up capital, while operators offering tokens backed by foreign currencies, such as dollar-pegged stablecoins, will need ₦15 billion. Other virtual asset service providers, including digital wallet, payment, transfer and custody businesses, must have at least ₦1 billion. The CBN said it may demand more capital from larger or riskier operators.
## Licensing and foreign firms

The rules make it illegal for individuals or companies to issue, exchange, distribute or facilitate regulated virtual assets in Nigeria without CBN approval. Foreign operators targeting Nigerian customers must incorporate and obtain licences locally, regardless of approvals elsewhere. Companies already licensed by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) will face extra capital requirements if they offer services under the CBN's oversight, while digital assets classed as securities will remain under SEC supervision. The rules also set standards for reserve management and consumer protection.
## Deadlines and fines

The regulations, released on Friday, give existing operators 30 days to register with the CBN, 60 days to begin submitting supervisory reports and 180 days to complete licence applications. Operators can continue at their current scale during the transition, but those who miss the deadline must suspend operations until licensed. Firms operating without approval face fines starting at ₦100 million.
## Background

Nigeria has one of the world's largest communities of cryptocurrency users. The CBN banned banks from dealing with crypto firms in 2021 before lifting the restriction in 2023, and the SEC has since moved to register and regulate crypto exchanges. Stablecoins, which are designed to keep a steady value linked to a currency such as the dollar, are widely used by Nigerians for savings and payments.

Naira-backed issuers need ₦10 billion.

stories.h: Obi asks Tinubu to account for subsidy savings and over $100bn in loans
stories.p: NDC candidate Peter Obi has challenged President Tinubu to explain what his government has done with the ₦15.8 trillion reportedly saved from fuel subsidy removal and more than $100 billion in borrowing, a day after Tinubu criticised Obi's record in Anambra.
body: Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), has called on President Bola Tinubu to account for money saved from the removal of the fuel subsidy and from government borrowing.
## What Obi said

In a statement on his X account on Saturday, 7 November 2026, titled 'Good Day, Mr President: Nigerians Deserve Accountability', Obi said the large sums flowing into government coffers, including higher tax revenues, should be producing clear improvements in Nigerians' daily lives. He urged the President to visit the remaining 33 states he has not yet toured, spend time with the people and explain what his administration had done with the ₦15.8 trillion he said had been saved from subsidy removal, the more than $100 billion he said had been borrowed, and increased revenue from taxes.
## The background to the exchange

Obi's statement came a day after Tinubu, speaking in Akwa Ibom, criticised the former Anambra governor's record on erosion in the state. At a reception in Uyo the same day, Tinubu said the naira would have become worthless without his reforms and that Nigeria would never go back to the subsidy. Vice-President Kashim Shettima also told an APC rally in Uyo that Obi had run himself out of the race.
## The figures

Obi did not give a breakdown of how he arrived at the figures. The World Bank reported this week that Nigeria's total external debt, including private-sector debt, rose to about $145 billion in 2025. The government says its borrowing is needed to fund infrastructure and that its reforms have saved the economy from collapse.
## What happens next
The Presidency had not publicly responded to Obi's statement at the time of writing. The presidential election is scheduled for 16 January 2027.
more: Obi cited ₦15.8 trillion in subsidy savings.
He said Tinubu had borrowed over $100 billion.

stories.h: Petrol prices at Lagos depots rise by up to ₦60 a litre as diesel falls
stories.p: Depot prices of petrol in Lagos rose by as much as ₦60 per litre this week, with several depots moving from ₦1,220 to ₦1,280, while diesel prices fell. The rise came despite a drop in global crude oil prices.
body: Petrol prices at major fuel depots in Lagos rose by as much as ₦60 per litre this week, while diesel prices fell, according to market data reported on Sunday, 8 November 2026.
## The figures

Between Monday and Friday, the average petrol price across seven comparable depots in Lagos rose by about ₦41 per litre, while diesel fell by about ₦33. Some of the biggest increases were recorded at African Terminal, Integrated and A.A. Rano, which each raised their prices from ₦1,220 to ₦1,280 per litre. Aiteo raised its price by ₦56 to ₦1,277, Rain Oil by ₦55 to ₦1,280 and Nipco by ₦29 to ₦1,279, while MRS Tincan cut its price by ₦30 to ₦1,280. Similar movements were seen at depots in Warri and Port Harcourt.
## Crude prices fell

The increases came even though international crude oil prices fell during the week, with Brent crude reportedly dropping by almost 5 per cent. Domestic supply conditions and marketers' costs also affect local prices.
## Background

Depot prices are what marketers pay before selling to motorists, so changes usually feed through to filling-station prices within days. Petrol prices are now set by the market after the removal of the fuel subsidy in 2023, and have fluctuated with competition between the Dangote refinery, NNPC and importers. President Bola Tinubu said in Uyo this week that the government will never return to the subsidy. Cooking gas prices have also reportedly risen to about ₦1,900 per kilogram.
## Cooking gas also up

Cooking gas prices have also risen. Retail prices reached about ₦1,800 per kilogram in Lagos and Ogun states after depot prices rose from ₦1,100 to as much as ₦1,445 per kilogram, an increase of about 31 per cent, according to reports on Sunday. Most depots were selling at ₦1,445, while Dangote's depot was selling at ₦1,150. At ₦1,800 per kilogram, refilling a 12.5kg cylinder costs about ₦22,500.
## Pump prices dip

By Monday, some pump prices had eased slightly. NNPC cut its Abuja price to ₦1,325 per litre after a price move by the Dangote refinery, and other Abuja outlets cut by about ₦10 to ₦1,410. In Lagos, MRS reduced its price from ₦1,350 to ₦1,331 and NNPC from ₦1,360 to ₦1,340, though prices in both cities remain above ₦1,300 per litre.
## What it means
Motorists may see higher pump prices in the coming days, while businesses that rely on diesel could get some relief.
more: Some depots raised petrol from ₦1,220 to ₦1,280 a litre.
Diesel prices fell during the week.
Global crude prices dropped.

stories.h: Flamingos beat Japan 2-1 to win Nigeria's first U-17 Women's World Cup
stories.p: Nigeria's Flamingos have won the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, beating Japan 2-1 in the final in Rabat, Morocco. Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku scored, making Nigeria the first African team to win the tournament.
body: Nigeria's under-17 women's team, the Flamingos, are world champions after beating Japan 2-1 in the final of the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in Rabat, Morocco, on Saturday, 7 November 2026.
## The match

Awawu Bashiru gave Nigeria the lead in the 39th minute at the Mohammed VI Football Complex, and Oluebube Umejiaku doubled the advantage two minutes after half-time, in the 47th minute. Japan pulled a goal back through Fuki Ito in the 80th minute, but the Flamingos held on to claim the trophy.
## History made

The victory makes Nigeria the first African country to win the competition, and gives the country its first FIFA world title in women's football at any level. Before this tournament, the Flamingos' best finish was third place in 2022. They reached the final by beating Brazil 3-1 in the semi-final, a match in which Bashiru also scored twice, while Japan beat North Korea on penalties in their semi-final.
## Background

Japan came into the final as one of the strongest teams in youth women's football, having won the tournament in 2014 and finished as runners-up in 2010 and 2016. CAF president Patrice Motsepe had travelled to Rabat to watch the final after praising the Flamingos for making Africa proud. Before the match, captain Harmony Chidi said the team was determined to bring the trophy home.
## What happens next
The win comes as the senior Super Eagles prepare for their AFCON qualifiers against Tanzania next week.
more: Nigeria beat Japan 2-1 in the final in Rabat.
Bashiru and Umejiaku scored for the Flamingos.
Nigeria are the first African winners of the tournament.

stories.h: Tinubu asks how Atiku built a university while he was vice-president
stories.p: At an APC rally in Port Harcourt, President Tinubu said he was cleaning up a mess created by people complaining about hunger, naming Atiku Abubakar, and questioned how the ADC candidate built a university while in office.
body: President Bola Tinubu has launched one of his sharpest attacks yet on Atiku Abubakar, presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC).
## What he said

Speaking at an All Progressives Congress (APC) rally in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, on Saturday, 7 November 2026, Tinubu dismissed critics who point to economic hardship under his government, saying he was cleaning up the mess left by those who came before him and that Atiku was one of them. He also questioned how Atiku had built a university while he was vice-president, a remark widely seen as raising questions about how the former vice-president acquired his wealth while in public office.
## Background

Atiku served as vice-president from 1999 to 2007 under Olusegun Obasanjo. He founded the American University of Nigeria in Yola, Adamawa State, and has long said his wealth comes from legitimate private business interests. He has repeatedly blamed Tinubu's policies, including the way fuel subsidy removal was handled, for rising prices. Tinubu's Rivers visit follows his trip to Akwa Ibom on Friday, where he said the naira would have become worthless without his reforms. FCT Minister Nyesom Wike, whose Rainbow Coalition backs the President, is a key ally in Rivers, and Governor Siminalayi Fubara has also declared support for Tinubu.
## Atiku replies

Later on Saturday, Atiku hit back in a statement issued by his campaign spokesman, Phrank Shaibu. He said his investment in education began long before he entered public office, when he laid the foundation for ABTI Academy in 1993, which later grew into the American University of Nigeria. In the same statement he referred to a 1993 US court forfeiture involving funds in an account linked to Tinubu, a matter the President's supporters have long said was a civil case that did not involve any criminal conviction. Atiku also said Tinubu's policies had pushed millions of Nigerians into extreme poverty, and rejected the President's claim that the economy is being rescued.
## What happens next
The presidential election is scheduled for 16 January 2027, and campaigns by all the major parties are expected to intensify in the coming weeks.
more: Tinubu spoke at an APC rally in Port Harcourt.
He said he was cleaning up a mess left by Atiku and others.
Atiku founded the American University of Nigeria in Yola.

stories.h: One dead, five injured as violence hits NDC rally in Asaba
stories.p: Delta police say one person died and five were injured in a clash during an NDC rally in Asaba on Saturday, after suspected thugs were filmed smashing supporters' vehicles. Police say organisers ignored advice to avoid a road procession.
body: Tension broke out at a rally of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Delta State on Saturday, 7 November 2026, after suspected thugs were reportedly filmed destroying vehicles belonging to party supporters.
## What happened

Footage shared on social media appears to show a group of men vandalising vehicles at or near the rally venue. According to reports, some NDC supporters retaliated after the attack, raising tensions further. It is not clear who the attackers were, how many vehicles were damaged or whether anyone was hurt. The police had not publicly commented on the incident at the time of writing.
## Police confirm one death

The Delta State Police Command later confirmed that one person died and five others were injured in a violent clash during the rally in Asaba, which was held in support of the NDC presidential candidate. Police spokesman SP Bright Edafe said the violence happened on Nnebisi Road at about 12.15pm. The command said it had received intelligence before the event that violence was possible, briefed the organisers and advised them to hold the rally at an approved venue rather than on the road, but that the procession went ahead. The injured were taken to hospital and an investigation has begun. Police Commissioner Samuel Erale condemned the violence and urged all parties to avoid road processions and inform the police before political gatherings. The identities of the victims had not been released.
## Background

The NDC is the party of presidential candidate Peter Obi and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso. Delta is governed by Sheriff Oborevwori, who joined the APC and has backed President Bola Tinubu's re-election. Political violence has already been reported on several sides ahead of the January 2027 elections: Obi's convoy was attacked in Calabar earlier this week, stones were thrown at a stage during a governor's campaign rally in Nasarawa, and APC supporters were attacked and a campaign vehicle burnt ahead of a rally in Katsina State last week. INEC has also warned of a plot to threaten and kidnap election workers.
## How people reacted
Many social media users condemned the violence and expressed concern for the safety of supporters at political events, while some warned that the same thugs could be used to disrupt the elections.
more: Suspected thugs reportedly destroyed NDC supporters' vehicles.
Some supporters were said to have fought back.
Police have not commented.

stories.h: Osimhen to have knee surgery, ruled out of Super Eagles' Tanzania qualifiers
stories.p: Galatasaray say Victor Osimhen needs arthroscopic surgery after a loose body was found in his left knee. He is expected to be out for two to four weeks, missing Nigeria's AFCON qualifiers against Tanzania.
body: Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen is set to undergo knee surgery, ruling him out of Nigeria's upcoming Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Tanzania.
## What happened

Galatasaray announced on Friday, 6 November 2026, that the 27-year-old needs arthroscopic surgery after medical checks found a loose body in his left knee. The problem was discovered after he played the full 90 minutes of the Turkish club's 2-0 Champions League win over VfB Stuttgart on Tuesday. The club said its doctor, Yener İnce, would carry out the operation at Maslak Acıbadem Hospital in Istanbul on Saturday, 7 November.
## How long he could be out

Arthroscopic surgery is a minimally invasive procedure that uses small cuts and a camera to treat problems inside a joint. According to reports, Osimhen is expected to be out for two to four weeks, which could mean a return in early to mid-December if there are no setbacks. Galatasaray have not given an official timeline and say they will assess his recovery in stages.
## Blow for the Super Eagles

The injury is a major blow for Nigeria, who face Tanzania twice in AFCON qualifying, including the match in Uyo on 13 November. Osimhen is the Super Eagles' main striker and one of Africa's most prolific forwards and was African Player of the Year in 2023. He was recently left off the shortlist for this year's CAF Player of the Year award.
## Squad named

On Saturday, Galatasaray said the operation had been successful and that Osimhen would be out for at least three weeks. Super Eagles coach Eric Chelle then named a 24-man squad for the two Tanzania matches without Osimhen. Goalkeeper Maduka Okoye was also left out by the coach's choice, with Stanley Nwabali, Arthur Okonkwo and the recalled Francis Uzoho named in goal. Midfielder Frank Onyeka was dropped, while Fisayo Dele-Bashiru, Tochukwu Nnadi and Yusuf Alhassan return. Wilfred Ndidi, Alex Iwobi, Ola Aina and Calvin Bassey are among those included.
## Background

Osimhen joined Galatasaray from Napoli and has been in strong form, with reports this week suggesting that a top Italian club is interested in signing him. His absence means the Super Eagles coaching staff will have to rely on other forwards for the Tanzania double-header.
more: A loose body was found in Osimhen's left knee.
He could be out for two to four weeks.
He will miss the AFCON qualifiers against Tanzania.

stories.h: Kunle Afod laments 20-minute wait for help after accident on Ibadan–Sagamu road
stories.p: Actor Kunle Afod says he witnessed a serious accident on the Ibadan–Sagamu Expressway and that no ambulance or emergency service arrived for about 20 minutes. He called on the authorities to improve emergency response on highways.
body: Nollywood actor Kunle Afod has called for better emergency services on Nigeria's highways after witnessing a serious accident on the Ibadan–Sagamu Expressway.
## What he said

In a video shared on social media on Saturday, 7 November 2026, the actor said he and others saw a terrible crash on the busy road, and that for about 20 minutes no ambulance or emergency responders came to help the victims. He described the situation as very sad and urged the relevant authorities to take urgent action so that accident victims receive timely medical help. He did not give details of how many people were involved or their condition.
## Background

The Lagos–Ibadan and Ibadan–Sagamu corridors are among the busiest roads in the country, and crashes are common. The Federal Road Safety Corps and state emergency agencies run ambulance services on some highways, but road users often complain that help arrives late, especially outside major cities. Afod has also been in the news this week after speaking publicly for the first time about his separation from his wife, Desola.
## Group disputes his account

On Saturday, a group called Ogun Crime Watch asked the police to question the actor over the video, which it described as misleading. The group said the crash, involving an 18-seater bus that reportedly burst a tyre and hit a concrete barrier near Saapade, happened on Friday, and that Ogun State emergency responders arrived at 12.28pm, one minute before Afod reportedly posted his video. It said 13 passengers were injured and taken to hospital, and accused the video of trying to make the state government look bad. Afod had not responded to the group's claims at the time of writing.
## Ogun government responds

The Ogun State Government also rejected the actor's account. In a statement on Saturday, the governor's special adviser on media, Kayode Akinmade, said a passer-by reported the crash at the Federal Road Safety Corps point in Ogere at 12.18pm, and that a state ambulance and FRSC officials reached the scene at 12.28pm, within 10 minutes. It said the state runs six ambulance points along the expressway, that its emergency call centre received no distress call about the crash, and that victims were taken to a hospital in Ogere, with the more seriously injured moved to Olabisi Onabanjo University Teaching Hospital in Sagamu. The statement accused the actor of framing the incident to damage the government.
## How people reacted

Many social media users agreed with the actor, saying faster emergency response could save lives, while others criticised the government for spending heavily on election campaigns while basic emergency services remain poor.
more: Afod says no help came for about 20 minutes.
The crash happened on the Ibadan–Sagamu Expressway.
He wants better emergency response on highways.

stories.h: Veteran Nollywood actor Diewait Ikpechukwu dies at 71
stories.p: Veteran Nollywood actor and former footballer Diewait Ikpechukwu has died at the age of 71 after a long illness, according to family sources. He was known for roles in classic films including August Meeting and Royal Palace.
body: Veteran Nollywood actor Diewait Ikpechukwu has died at the age of 71.
## What happened

According to family sources, the actor died on Thursday, 5 November 2026, after a prolonged illness. News of his death was reported on Friday. Further details about the circumstances of his death had not been made public at the time of writing, and the family had not announced funeral arrangements.
## His career

Before becoming an actor, Ikpechukwu was a professional footballer. He went on to have a long career in Nollywood and became a familiar face in classic Nigerian films. His film credits include 'August Meeting', 'Royal Palace', 'The Guilty', 'Across the River', 'Python King' and 'Ìjé Love', among many others.
## Family asks for privacy

On Saturday, 7 November, his daughter, lifestyle influencer Chiamaka Yusuf, asked the public, the media and the Actors Guild of Nigeria to allow the family to grieve privately, saying the family wanted to make any formal announcement about his death themselves. She asked for a burial poster circulating online to be taken down.
## Background
His death adds to a run of losses for Nollywood. The family of the late actor Francis Duru also recently announced burial arrangements for him.
more: Ikpechukwu died on Thursday after a long illness.
He was a former professional footballer.
He starred in films including August Meeting and Royal Palace.

stories.h: All 10 bus passengers kidnapped on Ijebu-Ode road freed, police say
stories.p: Ten passengers kidnapped from a commercial bus on the Ijebu-Ode–Ibadan road in Ogun State on 3 November, including a recently discharged corps member, have all been freed unharmed, police say. The kidnappers had reportedly demanded ₦25 million.
body: Gunmen have reportedly abducted 10 passengers travelling on the Ijebu-Ode–Ibadan road in Ogun State and are demanding ₦25 million for their release.
## What happened

The passengers were travelling in a commercial bus when armed men stopped the vehicle shortly after it passed through Ijebu-Ode on Tuesday, 3 November 2026, and took them into a nearby forest, according to reports on Friday. Two recently discharged members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) were said to be among the passengers; one escaped, while the other remains in captivity.
## Ransom demand

A relative of one of the victims said the incident was reported at a police station in Ijebu-Ode. She said the kidnappers later contacted the family using her brother's phone, first demanding ₦20 million and then raising it to ₦25 million. The Ogun State Police Command had not publicly commented at the time of writing.
## All passengers freed

Police later said all 10 passengers were released unharmed on the night of Saturday, 7 November, and that one suspected kidnapper was killed in a follow-up operation in which a rifle, ammunition and cash were recovered. Police did not say whether a ransom was paid.
## Background

Kidnapping on highways in the South-West has become a growing concern, with travellers on roads linking Ogun, Oyo and neighbouring states reporting attacks in recent years. Earlier this week, a court heard that suspects arrested over the abduction of corps members had admitted making confessional statements. Paying ransom is illegal in Nigeria, though families often say they feel they have no other choice.
## What happens next
Families of the victims are calling on the police and other security agencies to rescue the passengers.
more: Ten passengers were reportedly abducted on Tuesday.
A former corps member is among those held.
The kidnappers want ₦25 million.

stories.h: Power outages hit Lagos, Abuja and three other states as government blames gas shortages
stories.p: Residents of Lagos, Abuja, Ogun, Kwara and Oyo are facing worsening power cuts. Power Minister Joseph Tegbe has reportedly blamed gas shortages, maintenance work and low water levels at hydro plants, saying there has been no national grid collapse.
body: Electricity consumers in Lagos, Abuja, Ogun, Kwara and Oyo states are facing renewed power outages, prompting the federal government to explain the situation.
## What the minister said

Minister of Power Joseph Tegbe reportedly blamed the drop in supply on gas shortages, maintenance problems and reduced generation from hydropower plants because of low water levels, according to reports on Thursday, 5 November 2026. The government said there had been no major collapse of the national grid. It also said it had cleared 44 containers of equipment that had been stranded at the ports, which are needed to improve supply.
## Impact on customers

The outages have caused particular anger among Band A customers, who pay the highest tariffs in return for at least 20 hours of electricity a day. Ikeja Electric this week issued seven apologies in nine days for failing to meet that promise. Many households and businesses have had to spend more on fuel for generators.
## Public frustration

The outages have drawn complaints from well-known Nigerians. On Friday, comedian The Cute Abiola posted a video addressed to President Bola Tinubu, saying his solar system had run down after days of poor supply, that everywhere was hot and that the suffering was too much.
Actress Kate Henshaw also posted a video criticising the minister, saying power in her area lasts only minutes before going off and demanding accountability for spending on the sector.
## Grid operator explains

In a statement on Thursday, 5 November, the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO), which manages the national grid, blamed the drop in supply on inadequate gas deliveries to thermal power plants and lower water levels at hydroelectric stations. It said this had forced it to cut the power allocated to distribution companies, leading to more load shedding, and that the impact varies from one region to another.
## Minister gives timeline

In a further statement on Friday, 6 November, Minister of Power Joseph Tegbe said three problems had combined to cut supply: planned maintenance at the Egbin power station, limited gas supply to some thermal plants, and sabotage of key transmission lines, which he said had been especially damaging in Lagos because it blocked routes engineers would normally use to redirect power. He said damaged generating units would be brought back in phases, with the first expected back within 48 to 72 hours, and that work was under way with gas suppliers and on repairs. Singer Spyro also said on Saturday that when he visited an Eko Electricity Distribution Company office to complain, he found staff fanning themselves because of the heat.
## Agencies trade blame

By the weekend, agencies in the power sector were contradicting one another. NNPC's gas infrastructure subsidiary said in a statement dated Friday that its pipeline network had no constraints preventing gas from reaching power plants, rejecting suggestions that gas supply was to blame, though it said volumes actually taken up by individual plants and maintenance were separate issues. The Transmission Company of Nigeria also accused Ikeja Electric of misleading customers by blaming outages on 3 and 4 November on grid instability, saying its records showed no equipment failure or line trip, and that lower generation and problems within Ikeja Electric's own network were largely responsible.
## Supply restored in many areas

On Monday, 9 November, the Minister of Power said electricity had been restored to many of the affected areas in Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Kwara and the FCT, with work continuing on the rest. He said the vandalised Benin–Egbin 330kV line had been repaired, raising supply to the Lagos area to over 1,000 megawatts, back to the level before the disruption.
## Background

Nigeria's electricity supply has long been unreliable, with generation often far below demand for a population of more than 200 million. Gas supply problems, vandalism of pipelines and weak transmission infrastructure are frequent causes. The government says it is working to expand generation and transmission capacity, while critics, including opposition candidates, say progress has been too slow. Electricity is expected to be a major issue in the 2027 campaign.
## What happens next
Consumers are waiting for a clear timeline from the government and distribution companies on when supply will improve.
more: Outages are reported in Lagos, Abuja, Ogun, Kwara and Oyo.
The minister blamed gas shortages and low hydro output.
The government says there was no grid collapse.

stories.h: Court sacks ADC's David Mark-led leadership, voids Atiku's presidential nomination
stories.p: A Federal High Court in Abuja has reportedly removed the David Mark-led caretaker leadership of the ADC and nullified its decisions, including the nomination of Atiku Abubakar as presidential candidate. The ruling came a day after Atiku's Sokoto rally.
body: A Federal High Court in Abuja has removed the David Mark-led leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and voided its decisions, including the nomination of former vice-president Atiku Abubakar as the party's 2027 presidential candidate, according to reports on Thursday, 5 November 2026.
## The judgment

Justice Peter Lifu reportedly delivered the judgment in a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former national deputy chairman of the ADC for the North-East. The court ruled against the caretaker committee led by former Senate President David Mark and set aside all decisions it took on behalf of the party, which would include the primary that produced Atiku as candidate. Full details of the court's reasoning and any orders to INEC were still emerging.
## Timing
The ruling came less than 24 hours after Atiku formally launched his presidential campaign at a rally in Sokoto, which his campaign said drew a large crowd.
## Background

The ADC became the platform of a coalition of opposition figures in 2025, with David Mark as interim national chairman. Its leadership has faced legal challenges from former officials who say they were wrongly pushed aside. Several court cases over party primaries are ongoing across all major parties, and courts have recently sacked candidates in Nasarawa and ordered changes elsewhere.
## Atiku responds

In a statement issued from Birnin Kebbi on Thursday through his campaign spokesman, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku condemned the ruling and described it as a deliberate attempt to derail his campaign after the large turnout at his Sokoto launch. His campaign pointed to an earlier Federal High Court ruling that had dismissed a similar challenge to the David Mark-led leadership, and said the judgment would be challenged at the Court of Appeal. It said the campaign would continue, moving on to Kebbi State.
## Party and government react

The ADC's national publicity secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, described the judgment as legally indefensible and politically motivated, and said its timing, straight after the Sokoto rally, raised serious concerns. The party cited a ruling by another Federal High Court judge on 2 July 2026 that affirmed the David Mark-led leadership, and warned the APC against using the courts to eliminate competition. Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo welcomed the judgment, saying justice may be slow but is always sure, and rejected claims that it threatens democracy.
## What the judge ruled

According to further reports, Justice Lifu held that Mark's emergence as ADC chairman violated the party's constitution, the Electoral Act and the 1999 Constitution. The court also struck down the appointment of former Interior Minister Rauf Aregbesola as national secretary, along with other national officers and candidates the party had presented for 2027. Nafiu Bala Gombe, who filed the suit and leads a rival faction, praised the court for handling a politically sensitive case without outside influence.
## Atiku vows to stay in the race

On Friday, 6 November, Atiku declared that he would not step back from the 2027 presidential contest. He accused the Tinubu administration of using political pressure and court cases to weaken opposition parties, and alleged that there were attempts to compromise the voter register with AI-generated photographs and false identities, warning that Nigeria risked drifting towards a one-party system. He also criticised the government's handling of fuel subsidy removal, the fall of the naira and rising food prices. Separately, Shehu Sani, the APC senatorial candidate in Kaduna, advised the ADC to concentrate on appealing the ruling, saying the party was paying the price for taking over an existing, troubled party instead of registering a new one.
## INEC disowns fake poster

Also on Friday, INEC said a poster circulating on social media, which claimed the commission had reaffirmed the David Mark-led leadership of the ADC, was fake and did not come from it. The commission condemned the unauthorised use of its logo and of a photograph of National Commissioner Mohammed Haruna, and urged the public to rely only on its official channels.
## ADC files appeal

Later on Friday, the ADC said it had filed an appeal at the Court of Appeal against the judgment, together with an application for a stay of execution to halt any action based on it while the appeal is heard. The party said INEC was formally notified of both filings on 6 November. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, the party urged the commission not to take any action on the judgment until the stay application is decided, and asked its members and supporters to remain calm.
## Keyamo: ADC will be on the ballot

On Sunday, 8 November, Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo said on X that the ADC as a party would take part in the 2027 elections, arguing that the judgment affected only the faction led by David Mark, under which Atiku emerged as candidate, and not the party itself. He questioned why critics described the ruling as an attack on democracy, saying candidates who won primaries under the party's original leadership also had rights. Amaechi, Atiku's running mate, has warned that the ruling could cause unrest if it is not properly managed.
## INEC waits for judgment

INEC National Commissioner Mohammed Haruna said on Sunday that the commission would not act on the ruling until it had obtained and reviewed a certified true copy of the judgment, as it could not rely on media reports. He said the matter would be discussed at the commission's meeting next week, and that INEC would obey any court order arising from an appeal.
## ADC demands copy of judgment

On Monday, 9 November, the ADC called on the Federal High Court to release the judgment, saying paid applications for certified copies had gone unanswered although the judge said in open court that copies were ready. The party had earlier raised objections to Justice Lifu hearing the case, questioning his impartiality.
## ADC accuses chief judge of bias

On 10 November, the ADC campaign accused Chief Judge of the Federal High Court, Justice John Tsoho, of bias over the transfer of the case from Justice Emeka Nwite, who had already begun hearing it, to Justice Lifu, a move the party said it had formally opposed as forum shopping. The party urged the APC to face Atiku at the polls rather than in court. The court had not responded to the claims.
## Court rejected resignation letter

Details of the judgment published on Wednesday, 11 November, show that Justice Peter Lifu rejected a resignation letter the Mark-led faction had presented as evidence that the plaintiff, former deputy national chairman Nafiu Bala, had left his post. After comparing signatures, the judge found that the letter did not carry Bala's authentic signature. Bala had always insisted the letter was forged.
## Protest in Abuja
On Wednesday, Atiku's supporters gathered outside the Federal High Court in Abuja to demand the release of a certified true copy of the judgment, which the party needs for its appeal.
## What happens next
The ADC and Atiku are widely expected to appeal. Until the appeal is decided, it is not clear how the ruling will affect his candidacy or the party's campaign.
more: The court voided all decisions of the Mark-led caretaker committee.
That includes Atiku's nomination as presidential candidate.
An appeal is widely expected.

stories.h: Tinubu asks Senate to approve $7.7bn foreign borrowing for 2026 budget
stories.p: President Tinubu has asked the Senate to approve $7.7 billion in new external borrowing, about ₦10.79 trillion, mainly through Eurobonds and loans from international lenders. He said it would fund the 2026 budget and support the naira.
body: President Bola Tinubu has asked the Senate to approve fresh external borrowing of $7.7 billion to help finance the 2026 budget.
## The request

The request was contained in a letter read by Senate President Godswill Akpabio during plenary on Wednesday, 4 November 2026. At the budget exchange rate of ₦1,400 to the dollar, the amount is equal to about ₦10.79 trillion. According to the letter, the money would be raised mainly through Eurobond issuance, as well as loans from multilateral and bilateral lenders, international financial institutions and syndicated loans. The President said the borrowing would help finance the budget, strengthen foreign reserves and support the stability of the naira. He also asked the Senate to authorise the Minister of Finance and the Debt Management Office to carry out the plan.
## What the Senate did

Akpabio said the new request appeared to replace an earlier borrowing proposal and gave more detail on where the money would come from. He referred it to the Senate Committee on Local and Foreign Debts for consideration and a report.
## Background

Nigeria's public debt has risen sharply in recent years, and borrowing has become a major political issue ahead of the 2027 elections. Last week, former President Olusegun Obasanjo described the government's borrowing as 'absolute nonsense', while opposition candidates have warned that debt servicing is taking up too much of government revenue. The government says borrowing is needed to fund infrastructure and that its reforms have improved Nigeria's credit rating and ability to raise money abroad.
## Atiku urges rejection

ADC presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar has called on the Senate to reject the request. In a statement issued through his campaign spokesman, Phrank Shaibu, he warned against giving the government a blank cheque on foreign debt and urged senators to demand a full list of projects, the loan terms and a repayment plan before considering approval. His campaign noted that the request came before the National Assembly had finished considering an earlier external borrowing proposal of $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion.
## What happens next
The Senate committee is expected to review the request before the full Senate votes on it.
more: The request is worth about ₦10.79 trillion.
Funds would come mainly from Eurobonds and international loans.
The Senate referred it to its debt committee.

stories.h: VeryDarkMan dares Davido's camp to show proof of help, warns Zlatan
stories.p: VeryDarkMan has challenged Davido's associates to show receipts after a social media user claimed the singer once put him up in a Lagos hotel. He also warned Zlatan after Davido was filmed singing along to lyrics believed to target him at Zlatan's wedding party.
body: The feud between social media activist VeryDarkMan (VDM) and singer Davido has flared up again.
## The receipts challenge

On Wednesday, 4 November 2026, VDM shared on his Instagram stories a screenshot of a post by an X user who claimed Davido had once flown him to Lagos, put him up in a five-star hotel and helped him rise to fame. VDM reportedly dismissed the claim and dared Davido or his team to produce proof of any financial support.
## Warning to Zlatan

VDM also reacted angrily to a video from Zlatan Ibile's wedding welcome party in Morocco, in which Davido was seen singing along to lyrics from Zlatan's song 'Inferno', which fans believe is aimed at VDM. In a video, VDM criticised Davido and warned Zlatan that he would learn the hard way, saying he would not take the matter lightly. He also stood by recent controversial comments about his private life that had drawn reactions online.
## Background

VDM and Davido were once close, but their relationship broke down earlier this year. Davido recently unfollowed VDM on Instagram and publicly congratulated Zlatan on the success of 'Inferno', which topped the Apple Music Nigeria chart. Comedian GehGeh this week urged Carter Efe not to fight other people's battles amid the wider VDM controversy.
## Diss track

Later on Wednesday, VDM posted a studio preview of a new diss track aimed at Davido, titled 'On My Knees', which uses Zlatan's signature taglines and which he said would soon be released on streaming platforms.
## How people reacted
Fans were divided, with some backing VDM and others saying he should move on from the feud.
more: VDM dared Davido's team to show proof they helped him.
He warned Zlatan after Davido sang 'Inferno' lyrics.
The feud has run for months.

stories.h: Zlatan teaches father-in-law his famous legwork ahead of Marrakesh white wedding
stories.p: Singer Zlatan Ibile has gone viral after teaching his father-in-law his signature 'Gbeseh' legwork at a welcome party in Marrakesh, Morocco, ahead of his white wedding this weekend.
body: Street-pop star Zlatan Ibile has delighted fans with a video of him teaching his father-in-law his famous dance moves.
## What happened

The clip, which spread online on Tuesday, 3 November 2026, was reportedly filmed at a welcome party for family and friends in Marrakesh, Morocco, where Zlatan and his wife, Davita, are holding their white wedding this weekend. In the video, Zlatan takes to the dance floor with his wife's father and breaks into his trademark 'Gbeseh' legwork. The older man gamely copies the moves as guests cheer.
## Background

Zlatan and Davita recently held a high-profile wedding ceremony in Nigeria. The singer's new song 'Inferno', featuring Peruzzi and Shoday, recently topped the Apple Music Nigeria chart and has been seen as a response to activist VeryDarkMan, who criticised the wedding. Davido publicly congratulated Zlatan on the song's success.
## Davido on the dance floor
Davido was among the celebrities at the welcome party, and a video of him dancing between two female guests also went viral, drawing playful reactions from fans.
## The wedding
The white wedding took place in Morocco on Wednesday, 4 November. Davido attended with his wife, Chioma, who wore a pleated cape gown, while the singer wore a black tuxedo.
## Tears at the altar

A video from the white wedding in Marrakesh showed Zlatan in tears at the altar as the officiant opened the ceremony with a prayer, even before his bride walked in. The couple had already held a traditional wedding in Lagos on 24 October and a private civil ceremony. Guests in Morocco included Davido and Chioma, Carter Efe and Pretty Mike.
## How fans reacted

Fans praised the father-in-law for his enthusiasm and described the moment as heartwarming. Many said it showed a good relationship between Zlatan and his in-laws, and looked forward to seeing pictures from the white wedding.

Zlatan's white wedding takes place this weekend.

stories.h: Democrats projected to win both House and Senate in blow to Trump
stories.p: US networks are projecting that the Democrats have won control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the 2026 midterm elections. The party reportedly won Senate seats in states such as Texas, Iowa and Kansas, which Trump carried easily in 2024.
body: The Democratic Party is projected to have won control of both chambers of the United States Congress in the 2026 midterm elections held on Tuesday, 3 November, according to projections by US television networks reported early on Wednesday.
## The results

According to the projections, the Democrats have taken the House of Representatives and the Senate. The Senate results were described as particularly striking, with Democrats reportedly winning seats in states that President Donald Trump carried by wide margins in 2024, including Texas, South Carolina, Ohio, Kansas and Iowa. Texas had reportedly not elected a Democrat to statewide office since 1994. Final results in some races may take days to confirm.
## Why voters turned

Analysts have pointed to Trump's low approval ratings, voter anger over tariffs and inflation, and the long-running conflict with Iran as reasons for the swing. On the eve of the vote, US forces carried out limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island, while Trump told supporters that Iran might eventually have to be given 'the hammer'.
## Reactions

Trump sought to distance himself from the results, writing on social media that he was not on the ballot and that Republicans would have won in a landslide if he had been. He had held rallies in 20 states in the final weeks of the campaign. In a later interview, he said he was willing to accept the results and would look to work with the Democrats. Former President Barack Obama said voters had sent a clear message that they want politics that brings people together, and praised candidates who won in areas once seen as long shots. Among the night's firsts, Abdul El-Sayed became the first Muslim US senator, Keisha Lance Bottoms became the first Black woman elected governor of a US state, and Gina Hinojosa defeated Texas governor Greg Abbott.
## Trump on the Iran war

Speaking to reporters at the White House on Wednesday, Trump said it was largely true that the war with Iran had contributed to the Republican losses, as Vice President JD Vance had suggested, pointing to the rise in petrol prices it caused. He said he was not considering removing Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, and that he was open to working with Democrats as long as they were not destructive, adding that he still had the power to veto their bills.
## What it means

With control of both chambers, Democrats will be able to block much of the President's legislative agenda, launch investigations with the power to compel testimony, and hold up his nominees, including judges, during the last two years of his term. Trump remains president until January 2029.
## Why it matters for Nigeria

US policy on trade, aid and immigration affects Nigeria directly. A Democratic Congress could push back on measures such as visa restrictions and changes to trade programmes, including this week's decision to remove South Africa and Rwanda from the AGOA duty-free scheme. The White House had not formally responded to the projections at the time of reporting.
more: Democrats are projected to control both the House and Senate.
They reportedly won Senate seats in Texas, Iowa and Kansas.
Trump remains president until January 2029.
